2 · Palette

Categorical colours go to series in this fixed order, never cycled and never by rank. A single-series chart uses slot 1. Status colours (good / warning / danger) are the app's own and are never used as a series. Values are the app's --color-chart-* tokens for the theme shown.

Sequential · magnitude

One hue (slot 1) from the surface to full strength. Heatmaps and calendars.

near zero → most

Diverging · above / below a target

Blue and red with a neutral midpoint. Budget vs plan, change vs last period.

under plan ← on plan → over plan

Status · reserved, always with an icon or label

4 · The rules (DESIGN.md)

  • Native first. A table, list, KPI row or note is a native view; HTML is for charts and what native cannot draw.
  • Link the pack: _cinna/ui.css and _cinna/charts.js, never a chart library of your own unless the pack lacks the form.
  • No title inside the tile. The tile bar already shows it; a subtitle or a "vs last month" line is fine.
  • Tokens only. Every colour is a var(--cinna-*); no hex, no rgb, no named colours.
  • Colour by slot, in order. Up to 8 series; a 9th folds into "Other". Never two y-axes.
  • Text never wears a series colour. Identity comes from the swatch, line key or mark beside it.
  • Status colours mean status and always come with an icon, arrow or word.
  • A legend for two or more series; label selectively (the end, the max, the selection), never every point.
  • Fit the size. Small 3×2 is one number or one small chart; hide secondary parts with .cinna-hide-short / -narrow.
  • Empty, loading and notice states use .cinna-empty, .cinna-skeleton and .cinna-callout.
  • Selection and highlight go through the chart's select / highlight, and setContext after each.
  • Look at it in both themes before printing the reference.
